question: Three photos of the same shot in a men's singles match on a hard court, taken at the same instants by three different cameras (a broadcast camera behind the near baseline, a high side camera in the stands, and a low camera behind the far corner). In every photo the ball is shown at the same numbered instants, 60 ms apart (number 1 = earliest); the same number is the same instant in every photo. No camera positions or settings are given. ITF court dimensions (all measured to the OUTER edges of the lines): court 23.77 m long; singles sidelines 8.23 m apart; doubles sidelines 10.97 m apart; service lines 6.40 m from the net; centre service line on the court's long axis; baseline 10 cm wide, other lines 5 cm wide; net posts 1.07 m tall, their centres 0.914 m outside the doubles sidelines, on the line of the net; singles sticks 1.07 m tall, centred 0.914 m outside the singles sidelines; the net cord is 0.914 m high at the centre strap. The ball's diameter is 6.7 cm. The ball bounces once on the far side of the net. Treat the bounce as a single contact point directly below the ball's centre. What is the signed distance, in centimetres, from that contact point to the nearest OUTER edge of the singles court boundary (the far baseline or a singles sideline)? Positive if the contact point is inside the singles court, negative if it is outside. That is: min(distance inside the baseline, distance inside the sideline). Give a single number.
references: Hawk-Eye multi-camera triangulation (Owens, Harris & Stennett 2003, 'Hawk-Eye tennis system'); Hartley & Zisserman, Multiple View Geometry (DLT calibration, triangulation); ITF Rules of Tennis, Rule 1 (court) and Appendix I (ball)
